n.story:
Your role remains one of the most physically demanding and human-centric trades, but the 'prep and plan' phase of your week is undergoing a radical shift. Instead of spending hours on a ladder with a tape measure or squinting at paper blueprints, you will use AI-powered drones and computer vision to generate perfect 3D models of a roof in minutes. These tools will automatically identify wood rot, calculate precise material orders, and even flag potential safety hazards like weak structural points before you ever step foot on the shingles.

On the job site, your expertise shifts toward high-level problem solving and precision installation. While AI can't swing a hammer or navigate a steep pitch in the wind, it will act as a 'digital foreman' in your pocket, translating complex 2D architectural plans into augmented reality (AR) overlays that show you exactly where flashing and tiles should sit. You will spend less time on logistics and waste management and more time on the skilled craftsmanship that ensures a roof is weather-tight and durable.

Your role is shifting from a desk-bound administrator to a high-tech site conductor. In the past, you spent hours manually calculating quotes, juggling employee shifts, and squinting at 2D blueprints. Now, AI handles the heavy lifting of logistics. Automated systems monitor your stock levels in real-time and generate optimized crew schedules that account for weather patterns and individual skill sets, while computer vision tools instantly translate flat drawings into interactive 3D models. This automation doesn't replace you; it clears your schedule to focus on what happens on the roof.

With the administrative burden lifted, your value lies in 'augmented oversight.' You will use drones and AI-powered sensors to perform high-precision roof inspections, identifying wood rot or structural weaknesses that the naked eye might miss. You become a consultant on energy efficiency, using AI simulations to advise clients on the best materials for thermal performance. Your leadership is amplified as you use data-driven insights to mentor your team, focusing on safety and craftsmanship while the AI monitors compliance and project deadlines in the background.
auto: Employee shift scheduling and rotation planning
Inventory tracking and automated supply reordering
Drafting initial responses for requests for quotation
Manual data entry for work progress records
amp: High-precision thermal and structural roof inspections via drone-AI integration
Advanced energy performance modeling for sustainable building advice
Real-time hazard detection using AI-powered site surveillance
Predictive project management to preemptively resolve deadline bottlenecks
Data-backed employee performance coaching and skill-gap analysis
tools: AI-powered construction scheduling and ERP software
n.adv: Focus on mastering drone-based inspection tools and BIM software. Your future value depends on your ability to interpret AI-generated data to provide expert advice on building sustainability and complex safety management.

n.story:
Your role is evolving from a traditional installer to a high-tech energy systems architect. While the physical act of mounting panels remains a human-led task, the 'brain work' of the job is being supercharged. You no longer spend hours manually interpreting 2D blueprints or calculating load compatibilities; instead, you use AI-powered computer vision to scan a site and instantly generate optimized 3D wiring plans that maximize energy yield based on hyper-local weather patterns and material science data.

On-site, you are a technician augmented by intelligence. When troubleshooting a complex failure, AI-driven diagnostic tools analyze electrical signals in real-time to pinpoint the exact faulty component, often before you even open the control box. Your expertise shifts toward managing the integration of solar into smart grids and performing high-level mechanical optimizations that AI identifies through predictive maintenance sensors.
auto: Interpreting and converting 2D site plans into 3D models
Calculating electrical load and material compatibility
Monitoring regulatory compliance and safety documentation
Initial surface defect inspections of supplies
amp: Generative design for optimized photovoltaic system layouts
Predictive maintenance and advanced fault diagnostics
Real-time material interaction simulation
Augmented reality-guided complex electrical troubleshooting
Smart grid integration and energy flow optimization
tools: Generative CAD and solar design software
Computer vision for site assessment and defect detection
n.adv: Master AI-driven design and diagnostic software; the future of the trade isn't just in the tools you hold, but in the data you interpret.

neighbours.cat: Building and related trades workers, excluding electricians

n.story:
In your role, the physical 'craft' remains king, but your 'digital eyes' are getting a massive upgrade. While the manual labor of laying pipe and installing heads in cramped, unpredictable construction sites remains resistant to automation, the way you plan and verify your work is changing. AI now handles the tedious task of interpreting complex 2D blueprints, instantly converting them into 3D augmented reality overlays that you can view on-site. This ensures that every hanger and pipe is positioned perfectly the first time, eliminating costly rework.

Safety and compliance are also amplified. Wearable AI sensors can now monitor your environment for hazards and ensure that material compatibility—like checking for chemical reactions between specific pipes and sealants—is verified against massive databases in seconds. You are moving from a role of pure physical labor to one of a 'smart technician' who uses AI to navigate the increasing complexity of modern building codes and sophisticated fire suppression systems.
auto: Monitoring water pressure via IoT sensors
amp: Spatial reasoning through AR-guided installation
Real-time hazard detection and safety monitoring
Complex system troubleshooting via predictive diagnostics
Precision material selection for high-risk environments
Instant interpretation of updated building codes
n.adv: Get comfortable with Augmented Reality and digital plan-reading tools; being the person who can bridge the gap between digital designs and physical installation will make you indispensable.
